# Chapter Twenty-One: Judgment of Lobera

The compound descended into chaos.

Mercer, recovering from the initial flashbang glare, scrambled onto the flatbed of the compressor rig. His face was twisted with furious disbelief as he saw Victor carving through his elite strike force with ancient steel. "Fire on the descendant! Take him down! Don't let him reach the manifold!"

Three mercenaries opened fire from behind a tactical van, but before their rounds could converge on Victor, a guttural, rabid roar tore through the courtyard.

Brock erupted from the abbey ruins.

The rogue alpha was completely crazed, driven insane by silver burns, blood loss, and the agony of betrayal. Seeing Mercer on the compressor platform, Brock didn't care about the descendant or the wolves; he wanted to tear Mercer's throat out before he died. Brock lunged onto the flatbed, his massive claws slashing toward Mercer's face.

Mercer drew a heavy tactical sidearm loaded with high-grain silver hollow-points and fired three rounds into Brock's gut. The bullets exploded inside the beast's abdomen, flaring with searing chemical fire, but Brock's berserker rage carried him forward, his claws ripping across Mercer's tactical vest, shearing the kevlar and throwing the Captain off the platform onto the muddy gravel below.

Brock turned, foaming at the mouth, his amber eyes locking onto Victor.

"VANCE!" Brock bellowed, blood spraying from his lips. "IF I DIE TODAY, YOU DIE WITH ME!"

The eight-foot monstrosity leaped from the flatbed, descending on Victor with the full, crushing weight of a dying predator.

Victor didn't flinch. He didn't blink. The noise of the battlefield—the gunfire, the shouts, the howling wind—faded into complete silence. In his mind, three centuries of Toledo swordsmanship crystallized into a single, perfect sequence.

Victor stepped forward to meet the charge.

As Brock's massive right claw descended in a killing arc, Victor didn't parry the claw; he attacked the joint. With blinding, surgical precision, *Lobera* swept upward, severing the tendons in Brock's right wrist. In the same fluid motion, Victor stepped into the beast's guard, his left hand driving the Jamestown dagger deep into the nerve cluster beneath Brock's collarbone.

Brock let out a strangled, breathless wheeze, his massive limbs instantly losing their strength as the dagger's ancestral resonance paralyzed his motor nervous system. The behemoth fell to his knees on the gravel, staring up at Victor with fading, disbelieving eyes.

Victor stood over the rogue alpha, *Lobera* resting gently against the side of Brock's neck. The celestial steel hummed with soft, radiant light, burning away the taint of the silver poison.

"You threatened my family, Brock," Victor said softly, his voice devoid of anger, carrying only the absolute weight of justice. "You brought war to innocent people. By the authority of King Ferdinand and the First Covenant, your hunt is finished."

With a single, clean sweep, Victor ended the rogue alpha's life. Brock collapsed into the Highland turf, his body slowly relaxing as the rabid madness faded from his face, returning to the peaceful stillness of the earth.

"Gregory! The manual trigger!" Mercer's frantic voice screamed from beneath the transport rig.

Victor spun around. Mercer, battered and bleeding from his shredded tactical vest, had crawled to the manual emergency release valve on the side of the compressor. His hand was gripping the red pull-lever that would purge two hundred liters of pressurized Argentum-9 into the valley.

"You think you've won, boy?" Mercer spat, his eyes bulging with fanatical hatred. "You're a park ranger playing at being a king! These beasts are a plague! I'll wipe them out, and the Church will thank me for it!"

Mercer yanked the lever.

He was too late.

Victor didn't run; he leveled *Lobera* and spoke the third and final command word etched into the steel:

"*Shlama*!"

A blinding, concussive wave of azure energy exploded from *Lobera*'s tip. The kinetic pulse surged across the twenty feet separating them, striking the compressor's distribution manifold with the force of a pneumatic hammer.

The reinforced steel pipes were instantly crushed and severed. The release valve was sheared from its housing, collapsing the internal pressure chambers into a mangled knot of inert iron before a single molecule of the silver aerosol could escape. The pressurized gas back-vented harmlessly into the emergency containment bladder, sealed forever beneath the crushed metal.

Mercer was thrown backward by the shockwave, slamming against the rear wheel of the transport, his sidearm clattering into the mud.

Victor walked forward, his boots crunching in the gravel. He stopped three feet from the fallen Captain, *Lobera*'s glowing tip resting precisely at the hollow of Mercer's throat.

Mercer looked up, panting, terrified, staring into the face of the man he had intended to use as an expendable pawn. "Go on then..." Mercer whispered bitterly. "Strike me down. Prove you're just as bloodthirsty as the monsters you protect."

Victor looked down at him with cold pity. "My ancestor was an Arbiter, Mercer. Not an executioner. And I don't execute broken men."

With a sharp, dismissive motion, Victor flipped the sword, planting its point firmly into the turf beside Mercer's head.

From the southern ridge, the heavy, rhythmic thumping of twin turbine blades tore through the morning sky. Three black AgustaWestland transport helicopters bearing the official papal seal of the Holy See swept over the tree line, their landing lights illuminating the ruined abbey courtyard.

The rotors kicked up a gale of heather and mist as the helicopters touched down. The side doors slid open, and a dozen elite Swiss Guards in dark tactical attire deployed in a secure cordon.

Stepping out from the lead helicopter, flanked by two senior Vatican marshals, was Bishop Talbot.

The old bishop surveyed the carnage: the neutralized mercenaries, the shattered compressor rig, the fallen body of Brock, and the highland wolf families slowly emerging from the crypts, guided by Rebecca and Marcus.

Talbot walked toward the center of the courtyard, his eyes taking in the sight of Captain Mercer trembling on the ground, and Victor Vance standing tall, holding the ancient broadsword of King Ferdinand III.

Talbot stopped five paces away and slowly, reverently, bowed his head.
